styles.name: American Light Lager
text: Aroma: little to none; optional faint grainy/corn sweetness, trace spicy/floral hop. Flavor: neutral, crisp, dry; very low grainy/corn note; very low bitterness. Mouthfeel: very light, sometimes watery; very high carbonation, slight bite.
Lager yeast, clean (slight yeast character not a fault); no diacetyl/DMS mentioned; strong flavors = fault. Negligible hops. 2-/6-row barley with up to 40% rice/corn; enzymes may cut carbs.
Comparison: lighter, lower alcohol/calorie than American Lager; less hop/bitterness than German Leichtbier.
Commercial: Bud Light, Coors Light, Miller Lite, Michelob Light, Old Milwaukee Light.

styles.name: American Lager
text: Aroma: faint grainy/corn-sweet; optional light spicy/floral hop. Flavor: neutral, crisp dry finish; moderately-low to low grainy/corn; low to med-low bitterness; optional modest hop flavor. Mouthfeel: low to med-low body; very high carbonation, slight bite.
Lager yeast, clean; strong flavors = fault; light hopping; up to 40% rice/corn adjunct.
Comparison: more flavor/body than Light Lager; less bitterness/flavor than Intl Pale Lager; far less than European Pilsner.
Commercial: Budweiser, Coors Original, Miller High Life, Pabst Blue Ribbon, Old Style.

styles.name: Cream Ale
text: Aroma: low malt, sweet corn-like; low DMS optional; optional low hop (floral/spicy/herbal); low fruity esters optional. Flavor: neutral/grainy/crackery malt, low-moderate corny note, light DMS optional, well attenuated, dry-crisp to faintly sweet. Mouthfeel: light, crisp, smooth; high carbonation; body up to medium.

Clean ale yeast (or ale+lager mix); 6-row or 6-row/2-row; up to 20% maize in mash and up to 20% sugar in boil; any hops (often rustic American/continental). Commercial OG mostly 1.050-1.053, IBU rarely >20.
Comparison: more character than American Lager; lighter, smoother, more carbonated than Blonde Ale; can resemble a subtle Kolsch.
Commercial: Genesee Cream Ale, Little Kings Cream Ale, Sleeman Cream Ale, Sun King Sunlight.

styles.name: American Wheat Beer
text: Aroma: grainy/bready/doughy wheat; light malt sweetness ok; low-mod citrusy/spicy/floral/fruity hops (not typically dry-hopped); moderate esters optional but NO banana, NO clove phenols. Flavor: wheat bready/doughy, dry-crisp to moderately sweet; low-mod bitterness; low-mod hop flavor. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium; med-high to high carbonation; slight creaminess optional.
Clean American ale (or lager) yeast; German weizen yeast inappropriate. Wheat malt often 30-50%. American, German or New World hops. Brilliant or hazy both ok. American rye beers go in 31A.
Comparison: more hops, less yeast character than Weissbier; same range/balance as Blonde Ale but wheat-led.
Commercial: Bell's Oberon, Boulevard Unfiltered Wheat, Goose Island 312 Urban Wheat, Widmer Hefeweizen.

styles.name: International Pale Lager
text: Aroma: low to med-low grainy/slightly corny malt; very low-medium spicy/floral/herbal hop. Flavor: low-moderate grainy malt, med-low to medium bitterness, crisp dry well-attenuated finish; optional corny sweetness; neutral aftertaste. Mouthfeel: light-medium body; mod-high to high carbonation, slight bite.
Clean lager yeast; 2-/6-row; rice/corn/sugar allowed but generally all-malt; skunkiness in commercial beers = handling fault. Entrant may specify regional variant (Mexican lager etc.).
Comparison: more bitter/filling than American Lager; less than German Pils; less body/malt/hop than Czech Premium Pale; robust versions near Helles but with adjunct quality.
Commercial: Heineken, Corona Extra, Asahi Super Dry, Red Stripe, Singha, Birra Moretti.

styles.name: International Amber Lager
text: Aroma: low-mod grainy malt with caramel/toasty accents, occasionally nutty/biscuity, never roasty; low floral/spicy hops. Flavor: low-mod malt with caramel or toasty-bready notes; optional low corny sweetness; low-mod bitterness; moderately dry, malty aftertaste. Mouthfeel: light-medium, smooth, medium to high carbonation, sometimes slightly creamy.
Clean lager yeast; 2-/6-row, caramel/Victory/amber/roast malt; adjuncts, sugar or coloring possible; European or American hops.
Comparison: less malt development than Vienna Lager (adjunct taste); less robust/bitter than Altbier.
Commercial: Yuengling Lager, Brooklyn Lager, Abita Amber, Dos Equis Amber, Capital Wisconsin Amber.

styles.name: International Dark Lager
text: Aroma: faint malt; optional med-low roast/caramel; light hops optional. Flavor: low-med sweet maltiness, optional caramel/roast with coffee/molasses/brown sugar/cocoa hints; low-med bitterness; very light fruitiness possible; moderately crisp; burnt or strong roast inappropriate. Mouthfeel: light to med-light, smooth, light creaminess; medium to high carbonation.
Clean lager yeast; corn/rice/sugar adjuncts typical; light caramel/dark roast malts; coloring agents may be used.
Comparison: less flavor/richness than Munich Dunkel or Schwarzbier.
Commercial: Baltika #4, Shiner Bock, Heineken Dark, San Miguel Dark, Dixie Blackened Voodoo.

styles.name: Czech Pale Lager
text: Aroma: light-mod bready-rich malt + light-mod spicy/herbal (Saaz-type) hops; faint caramel ok; light non-intrusive diacetyl and light fruity esters optional; no sulfur. Flavor: med-low to medium bready malt, rounded hoppy finish; prominent but never harsh bitterness. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, moderate carbonation.
Czech Pilsner malt, Czech hops, Czech lager yeast, soft water. Most-consumed beer in Czechia.
Comparison: lighter, lower-intensity everyday version of Czech Premium Pale Lager.
Commercial: Bernard svetle 10, Radegast Razna 10, Primator Antonin, Unetice 10, Breznak.

styles.name: Czech Premium Pale Lager
text: Aroma: medium to med-high bready-rich malt with med-low to med-high spicy/floral/herbal hops; light diacetyl or very low fruity esters optional. Flavor: rich complex bready malt, pronounced yet soft rounded bitterness, floral/spicy hop flavor, long finish balanced between malt and hops; light to moderately-low diacetyl and low hop-derived esters acceptable. Mouthfeel: medium body; moderate to low carbonation.
Czech malt/hops/yeast; low-sulfate/carbonate soft water; decoction traditional. Unfiltered kvasnicove (yeast beer) versions exist. Only Pilsner Urquell and Gambrinus called "Pilsner" in Czechia.
Comparison: more color, malt richness, body, fuller/softer than German Pils; stronger than Czech Pale Lager.
Commercial: Pilsner Urquell, Budvar 33, Bernard Svateční lezak, Unetice 12, Primator Premium, Radegast Ryze horka 12.

styles.name: Czech Amber Lager
text: Aroma: moderate rich malt, bready/Maillard-dominant or caramel-sweet; spicy/floral hops moderate to none; low stone-fruit/berry esters possible; low diacetyl optional. Flavor: medium to med-high complex malt (dry-Maillard to caramelly, sometimes graham-cracker), low-mod spicy hops, clean prominent bitterness; subtle plum/berry esters and low diacetyl optional; no roast. Mouthfeel: medium-full to medium, soft, gently creamy, moderate to low carbonation.
Pilsner + caramel malts (Vienna/Munich possible), Czech hops/yeast, soft water.

Comparison: like Vienna Lager but stronger Czech late-hop; or a richer, caramelly British Bitter; big-brewery versions resemble Premium Pale with darker malt, small breweries more hop/malt complexity or sweetness.
Commercial: Kozel Semi-Dark, Bernard Jantarovy lezak, Gambrinus Polotmava 12, Primator polotmavy 13, Lobkowicz Demon 13.

styles.name: Czech Dark Lager
text: Aroma: med to med-high rich, sometimes sweet malt (bread crust, toast, nuts, cola, dark fruit, caramel); roast (chocolate/sweet coffee) none-moderate; low-mod spicy hops optional; low diacetyl and low-mod plum/berry esters may occur. Flavor: medium to med-high deep malt dominates, Maillard richness, light-mod residual sweetness, very low-mod roast; low-mod spicy hop; moderate to med-low but perceptible bitterness; low-mod diacetyl and light esters possible. Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full, moderately creamy, smooth; moderate-low carbonation; stronger versions slightly warming.
Pilsner + dark caramel malts, debittered roast; Vienna/Munich ok; Czech hops/yeast; soft water. Traditional versions ~18-20 IBU and sweeter; modern drier/more bitter.
Comparison: Czech equivalent spanning Munich Dunkel to Schwarzbier, but richer malt and more hop aroma/flavor/bitterness.
Commercial: U Fleku Flekovsky tmavy 13, Kozel Dark, Krusovice cerne, Budvar tmavy lezak, Bernard cerny lezak 12, Herold tmave silne 13.

styles.name: Munich Helles
text: Aroma: moderate grainy-sweet malt; low to mod-low spicy/floral/herbal hop; clean. Flavor: moderately malty start suggesting sweetness, soft rounded palate, low to med-low bitterness, soft dry finish (not crisp); malt dominates hops but hops noticeable; no real residual sweetness. Mouthfeel: medium body, medium carbonation, smooth, well-lagered.
Continental Pilsner malt, German hops, clean German lager yeast. (Helles Lagerbier.)
Comparison: Dunkel-like balance but pale/less sweet; more body/malt than German Pils; fewer hops and slightly less ABV than Exportbier; less body/alcohol than Festbier.
Commercial: Augustiner Lagerbier Hell, Spaten Munchner Hell, Paulaner Munchner, Weihenstephaner Original, Hacker-Pschorr Munchner Gold.

styles.name: Festbier
text: Aroma: moderate malty richness, toasty-doughy, impression of sweetness; low to med-low floral/herbal/spicy hops; not deeply toasted/caramel/biscuity; clean. Flavor: medium to med-high lightly toasty bread-dough malt, med to med-low bitterness, malty balance, well-attenuated and crisp but not dry; med-low to medium hop flavor. Mouthfeel: medium, smooth, somewhat creamy, medium carbonation; alcohol barely warming.
Mostly Pils malt with some Vienna/Munich; German lager yeast. Gold, no amber hues; modern Oktoberfest beer (Wiesn); "Oktoberfestbier" is a protected term.
Comparison: less intense/toasty than Marzen; stronger than Helles with more body/hop/malt; less rich than Helles Bock; malt complexity like a high-gravity Czech Premium Pale without the hops.
Commercial: Paulaner Oktoberfest Bier, Hofbrau Oktoberfestbier, Augustiner Oktoberfest, Weihenstephaner Festbier, Hacker-Pschorr Superior Festbier, Lowenbrau Oktoberfestbier.

styles.name: Helles Bock
text: Aroma: mod to strong grainy-sweet malt with light toast and Maillard; mod-low spicy/herbal/floral hop optional; clean; low esters and light alcohol optional. Flavor: mod to mod-strong grainy-sweet/doughy/bready/lightly toasty malt with some Maillard; moderate bitterness (hoppier than other bocks); optional low-mod hop flavor; well-attenuated, moderately dry finish. Mouthfeel: medium body, mod to mod-high carbonation, smooth, light warming optional.
Pils/Vienna/Munich malts, no adjuncts, light pale crystal possible; German hops; clean lager yeast; decoction traditional but with less boiling to limit color; soft water.
Comparison: pale Dunkles Bock, or Helles/Festbier at bock strength; drier, hoppier than Dunkles Bock; weaker than pale Doppelbock.
Commercial: Ayinger Maibock, Hofbrau Maibock, Einbecker Mai-Urbock, Mahr's Heller Bock, Hacker-Pschorr Hubertus Bock, Altenmunster Maibock.

styles.name: German Leichtbier
text: Aroma: low-med spicy/herbal/floral hop; low to med-low grainy-sweet/crackery malt; clean. Flavor: low-med grainy-sweet malt, medium bitterness, low-med hop flavor, dry finish. Mouthfeel: light to very light, medium to high carbonation, smooth.
Pils malt, German lager yeast and hops. Schankbier gravity class; diet-oriented. Leicht variants of wheat/Kolsch/Alt go to 34B.
Comparison: lighter, slightly less aggressive German Pils/Helles; more bitter and flavorful than American Light Lager.
Commercial: Greif Brau Leicht, Schonramer Surtaler Schankbier, Mullerbrau Heimer Leicht, Waldhaus Sommer Bier, Autenrieder Schlossbrau Leicht.

styles.name: Kolsch
text: Aroma: low grainy-sweet malt; subtle optional apple/pear/cherry fruit; low floral/spicy/herbal hop optional; clean, fresh. Flavor: delicate balance of malt, fruitiness, hops; med-low to medium bitterness; soft, rounded, dry slightly crisp finish; no real residual sweetness; no component strong. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium (mostly med-light), medium to med-high carbonation, smooth, soft.

TOP-fermented (clean attenuative German ale yeast, ~15 C), then cold conditioned near freezing up to a month; Pils/Pale/Vienna malt, occasional wheat; German hops. Protected appellation (Kolsch Konvention 1986). Oxidation-prone; served in a Stange.
Comparison: can be mistaken for Cream Ale or a subtle German Pils.
Commercial: Fruh Kolsch, Gaffel Kolsch, Reissdorf Kolsch, Paffgen, Sunner, Mulhen, Sion.

styles.name: German Helles Exportbier
text: Aroma: med-low to medium floral/spicy/herbal hop; moderate grainy-sweet malt (light toasty/bready/doughy); clean; malt and hops balanced. Flavor: moderate balanced malt and hops, medium noticeable bitterness, full palate, medium-dry finish; mineral character as roundness and dry flinty finish; background sulfate optional. Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full, medium carbonation, smooth; slight warmth in stronger versions.
Mineral water (high sulfate, carbonate, chloride); Pils malt; German/Czech hops; German lager yeast; decoction traditional.
Comparison: fewer finishing hops and more body than Pils; more bitter and drier than Helles; stronger, drier, less hoppy than Czech Premium Pale.
Commercial: DAB Dortmunder Export, Dortmunder Kronen, Schonramer Gold, Chuckanut Export Dortmunder, Landshuter Edel Hell, Mullerbrau Export Gold.

styles.name: German Pils
text: Aroma: mod to mod-high floral/spicy/herbal hops; low-med grainy/doughy malt with honey/toasted cracker; clean. Flavor: malt quickly overtaken by hop flavor and bitterness, dry crisp finish; medium to high lingering bitterness; mineral water lengthens dryness; always bitter-balanced. Mouthfeel: medium-light, medium to high carbonation, may be flinty/minerally.
Continental Pils malt, German hops, clean German lager yeast. Paler, drier, sharper, more bitter going north; Bavarian versions softer.
Comparison: lighter, drier, crisper, more bitter, more carbonated than Czech Premium Pale; more hop/malt/bitterness than Intl Pale Lager; more hop and drier than Helles.
Commercial: Jever Pilsener, Konig Pilsener, Trumer Pils, Rothaus Pils, Schonramer Pils, Paulaner Pils, Bierstadt Slow Pour Pils, ABK Pils Anno 1907.

styles.name: Marzen
text: Aroma: moderate rich bready, toasty malt, light bread crust; very low hop optional; clean lager; caramel-sweet, biscuity-dry, roasted aromas inappropriate. Flavor: moderate to high rich malt, initial sweetness but moderately-dry to dry finish; bready/toasty complexity; moderate bitterness; low-none hop flavor; sweet caramel, dry biscuit, roast inappropriate. Mouthfeel: medium, smooth, creamy; medium carbonation; fully attenuated, not cloying.
Munich-malt emphasis, finest base malts; decoction traditional; German lager yeast. Orange-amber to reddish-copper (not golden).
Comparison: not as strong/rich as Dunkles Bock; more malt depth/body and slightly fewer hops than Festbier; less hoppy but as malty as Czech Amber.
Commercial: Paulaner Oktoberfest, Hacker-Pschorr Oktoberfest Marzen, Weltenburg Kloster Anno 1050, Hofmark Marzen, Saalfelder Ur-Saalfelder.

styles.name: Rauchbier
text: Aroma: blend of beechwood smoke (smoky/woody/bacon-like, subtle to strong) and malt (low-mod, toasty); smoke and malt often inversely related; low hop optional; clean. Flavor: follows aroma, smoke low to high yet harmonious with Marzen-like toasty malt; medium-dry to dry finish; moderate balanced bitterness; up to moderate hop flavor; harsh/acrid/burnt/rubbery/creosote smoke inappropriate; ham/bacon ok if not greasy. Mouthfeel: medium, medium to med-high carbonation, smooth; no astringent phenolic harshness.
Marzen-type grist + sizeable German Rauchmalz (beechwood-smoked Vienna-type); lager yeast; German/Czech hops. Bamberg specialty. Other smoked German styles go to 32A.
Comparison: Marzen with balanced sweet smoke and somewhat darker color.
Commercial: Schlenkerla Rauchbier Marzen, Spezial Rauchbier Marzen, Goller Rauchbier, Rittmayer Rauchbier, Cervejaria Bamberg.

styles.name: Dunkles Bock
text: Aroma: med to med-high rich bready malt, Maillard/toasty; virtually no hop aroma; some alcohol; clean (slight dark fruit allowed). Flavor: med to med-high complex malt dominated by toasty Maillard, some dark caramel; bitterness only supports malt, lingering malty sweetness but well-attenuated; no hop flavor; no roast, burnt or dry biscuit. Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full, mod to mod-low carbonation, alcohol warmth never hot, smooth.
Munich and Vienna malts, tiny dark roast for color at most, no adjuncts; continental hops; clean lager yeast; decoction important.
Comparison: darker, richer, less bitter than Helles Bock; less alcohol/richness than Doppelbock; stronger than Marzen; richer, less attenuated, less hoppy than Czech Amber.
Commercial: Einbecker Ur-Bock Dunkel, Aass Bock, Kneitinger Bock, Schell's Bock, Penn Brewery St. Nikolaus Bock, Lindeboom Bock.

styles.name: Vienna Lager
text: Aroma: moderate malt, toasty and malty-rich; floral/spicy hop low to none; clean; significant caramel/biscuit/roast inappropriate. Flavor: soft elegant malt, rich toasty without significant caramel/biscuity/roast; firm bitterness for balanced, fairly dry soft finish; low-none hop flavor. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, gentle creaminess, moderate carbonation, smooth.
Best-quality Vienna malt (also Pils/Munich), continental hops, clean German lager yeast; small specialty malt for color. Standard-strength everyday beer.
Comparison: Marzen-like malt but lighter, slightly more bitter/dry, lower ABV; less rich/malty/hoppy than Czech Amber.
Commercial: Ottakringer Wiener Original, Schell's Firebrick, Devils Backbone Vienna Lager, Figueroa Mountain Red Lager, Heavy Seas Cutlass, Chuckanut Vienna, Theresianer Vienna.

styles.name: Altbier
text: Aroma: malty, baked bread/nutty toasted crust, no roast/chocolate; moderate to mod-high malt; mod-low spicy/peppery/floral hops; very clean fermentation, low to med-low esters optional. Flavor: similar malt; assertive medium to high bitterness; medium-dry to dry, long grainy-bitter malty aftertaste, nutty or bittersweet; light dark-fruit esters possible; medium to low spicy hop; light mineral optional; no roast. Mouthfeel: medium body, smooth, medium to med-high carbonation, low astringency.

TOP-fermented clean attenuative ale yeast at cool temps, then cold-conditioned; Pils (sometimes Munich) with small crystal/chocolate/black, optionally wheat; Spalt hops traditional; step mash traditional. Dusseldorf. Most examples 25-35 IBU. Sticke/doppelsticke go to Cat 27.
Comparison: more bitter and malty than Intl Amber Lager; similar in technique/flavor/color to California Common; less alcohol/richness than Dunkles Bock; drier, richer, more bitter than Vienna.
Commercial: Uerige Altbier, Fuchschen Alt, Diebels Alt, Schumacher Alt, Original Schlussel Alt, Bolten Alt, Schlosser Alt.

styles.name: Munich Dunkel
text: Aroma: moderate to high malt richness like toasted bread crust with hints of chocolate, nuts, caramel, toffee; malty-rich more than sugary; clean; light hop optional. Flavor: medium to high rich malt as aroma; med-low to medium bitterness, malty balance; soft, not overly sweet, medium-dry finish; no roast/burnt/bitter malt, no harsh dry grain, caramel not sweet. Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full, soft dextrinous, moderate carbonation, smooth, not warming.
Munich malts (Pils/Vienna ok), light specialty malts; decoction traditional; German hops and lager yeast. Franconian versions more bitter.
Comparison: less intense/strong than Dunkles Bock; lacks roast and often bitterness of Schwarzbier; richer, more malt-centric, less hoppy than Czech Dark Lager.
Commercial: Ayinger Altbairisch Dunkel, Ettaler Kloster-Dunkel, Hacker-Pschorr Munchner Dunkel, Hofbrauhaus Dunkel, Weltenburger Kloster Barock-Dunkel, Eittinger Urtyp Dunkel.

styles.name: Schwarzbier
text: Aroma: low-mod malt (clean/neutral to bready, hint of dark caramel) with hints of roast (dark chocolate/coffee-like, never burnt); mod-low hop optional; clean lager. Flavor: light-mod malt; light-mod roast giving bitter-chocolate but never burnt; med-low to medium bitterness; light-mod spicy/floral/herbal hop; dry finish; some residual sweetness acceptable but not traditional; subtle roast in aftertaste. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, mod to mod-high carbonation, smooth, no harshness/astringency.
Munich and Pilsner base, huskless dark roasted malts; German hops; clean lager yeast. Porter-like strong roast is a flaw. "Black Pils" is rarely as dark or bitter as that.
Comparison: vs Dunkel: darker, drier, lighter body, noticeable roast edge; not an American Porter with lager yeast; drier, less malty, less hoppy than Czech Dark Lager.
Commercial: Kostritzer Schwarzbier, Kulmbacher Monchshof Schwarzbier, Chuckanut Schwarz, Devils Backbone Schwartz Bier, pFriem Schwarzbier, Nuezeller Original Badebier.

styles.name: Doppelbock
text: Aroma: very strong maltiness, light caramel, up to moderate alcohol; virtually no hop aroma. Dark: rich Maillard, deeply toasted, slight chocolate (never roasted/burnt), mod-low dark fruit (plum, grape, fruit leather). Pale: strong toasty malt, possible light floral/spicy/herbal hop accent. Flavor: very rich malty; moderate to mod-low bitterness letting malt dominate; faint hop flavor optional; malty-sweet palate but attenuated finish (sweetness from low hopping, not incomplete fermentation); clean. Pale: bready/toasty, drier. Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, mod to mod-low carbonation, very smooth, light alcohol warmth never burning.
Pils/Vienna/Munich malts, occasional dark malt for color; German hops; clean lager yeast; decoction traditional. No upper gravity limit if balance holds. "-ator" names (Salvator trademark history).
Comparison: stronger, richer, fuller version of Dunkles or Helles Bock; pale ones more attenuated, less dark-fruit.

Commercial: Dark - Paulaner Salvator, Ayinger Celebrator, Spaten Optimator, Weihenstephaner Korbinian, Andechs Doppelbock Dunkel, Troegs Troegenator; Pale - Plank Bavarian Heller Doppelbock, Meinel Doppelbock Hell, Eggenberg Urbock 23, Riegele Auri.

styles.name: Eisbock
text: Aroma: rich intense malt (bready, toasty, caramel, faint chocolate, dark fruit like plum/grape) with definite alcohol, not harsh/solventy; no hop aroma; clean. Flavor: rich sweet malt balanced by significant alcohol; Maillard, toasty, caramel, dark-fruit esters possible; bitterness just offsets sweetness; no hop flavor; finish rich with dryness from alcohol, not sticky/syrupy. Mouthfeel: full to very full, low carbonation, significant warmth without sharp heat, very smooth/silky; head retention moderate to poor; pronounced legs.

Made by freeze concentration ("freeze distillation") of a doppelbock-like beer, removing ice; concentrates flavors AND any defects; extended lagering afterward to smooth. Concentrated roughly 7-33% by volume. Name refers to process, not alcohol (some Doppelbocks are stronger).
Comparison: not simply a stronger Doppelbock; not as thick/rich/sweet as Wheatwine.
Commercial: Kulmbacher Eisbock.

styles.name: Baltic Porter
text: Aroma: rich malt (caramel, toffee, nuts, deep toast, licorice); complex moderate alcohol/ester (plums, prunes, raisins, cherries, currants, sometimes vinous/Port-like); dark chocolate/coffee/molasses, never burnt; no hops; no sourness. Flavor: rich malt, dried-fruit esters, alcohol; prominent but smooth Schwarzbier-like roast stopping short of burnt; malty-sweet start, darker malt dominates, dryish finish with coffee/licorice/dried fruit; med-low to medium bitterness; hop flavor none to med-low; clean. Mouthfeel: quite full-bodied and smooth, well-aged warmth, medium to med-high carbonation.

Generally LAGER yeast (cold-fermented if ale yeast, e.g., Russia); debittered dark malt; Munich/Vienna base; continental hops; crystal/adjuncts possible. Historically top-fermented; modern name since 1990s. Most commercial 7-8.5% ABV.
Comparison: combines Doppelbock body/richness, English Porter dark malt, Schwarzbier roast, Old Ale alcohol/fruitiness; far less roasted and often weaker than Imperial Stout.
Commercial: Zywiec Porter, Okocim Mistrzowski Porter, Baltika #6 Porter, Sinebrychoff Porter, Aldaris Mezpils Porteris, Devils Backbone Danzig.

styles.name: Weissbier
text: Aroma: moderate to strong banana (esters) and clove (phenols), usually stronger than malt; light-mod bready/doughy wheat; light vanilla optional; light hops optional; bubblegum, sourness, smoke = faults. Flavor: low to moderately strong banana and clove, balanced; soft bready/doughy wheat; very low to mod-low bitterness; relatively dry finish (perceived sweetness from low bitterness, sweet/heavy finish is a flaw). Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, fluffy creamy then spritzy; high to very high carbonation.
Weizen yeast, cool fermentation; wheat at least half of grist; Pils malt; decoction traditional. Hefeweizen; Kristall = filtered. Entrant may say if yeast roused.
Comparison: vs American Wheat has banana/clove and less bitterness; vs Dunkles Weissbier paler, less malt richness.
Commercial: Weihenstephaner Hefeweissbier, Schneider Weisse Original, Ayinger Brau-Weisse, Hacker-Pschorr Hefeweissbier, Hofbrauhaus Munchner Weisse, Distelhauser Hell Weizen.

styles.name: Dunkles Weissbier
text: Aroma: moderate banana and clove balanced with malt; light-mod bready/doughy wheat with caramel/bread crust/richer malt; low-mod vanilla optional; bubblegum, sourness, smoke = faults. Flavor: low to moderately strong banana/clove (malt may mask clove); low to med-high wheat with caramel/toast/bread crust; no strong roast (touch of roasty dryness ok); very low to low bitterness; relatively dry finish. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium-full, fluffy-creamy, moderate to high carbonation.
Weizen yeast, cool fermentation; wheat at least half; Munich/Vienna/Pils malt plus dark/caramel wheat or color malt; decoction traditional.
Comparison: Weissbier yeast/wheat with Munich Dunkel malt richness; banana-clove less apparent than Weissbier; similar yeast to Roggenbier without rye.
Commercial: Weihenstephaner Hefeweissbier Dunkel, Franziskaner Hefe-Weisse Dunkel, Ayinger Ur-Weisse, Ettaler Benediktiner Weissbier Dunkel, Tucher Dunkles Hefe Weizen, Hirsch Dunkel Weisse.

styles.name: Weizenbock
text: Aroma: medium-high to high malty richness with bready/grainy wheat; medium-low to med-high weizen yeast (banana, clove); vanilla optional; no hops; low-mod alcohol, not hot; bubblegum, sourness, smoke = faults. Dark: deeply toasted/Maillard like Dunkles Bock/dark Doppelbock, caramel, dark fruit (plum, prune, raisin) esp. with age. Pale: grainy-sweet bready toasty like Helles Bock/pale Doppelbock. Flavor: medium-high to high malt richness with bready wheat; low-mod banana and spice; no hop flavor; low to med-low bitterness, slightly sweet impression but finishes dry; complexity improves with age. Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, soft, fluffy/creamy, mild warmth, moderate to high carbonation.
Weizen yeast, cool fermentation; wheat at least half; Munich/Vienna/Pils malt; sparing color malts; decoction traditional. Bock to Doppelbock strength. Late- or dry-hopped versions go to 34B.
Comparison: stronger/richer than Weissbier or Dunkles Weissbier with similar yeast; analogous to pale/dark Doppelbock.

Commercial: Dark - Schneider Weisse Aventinus, Plank Bavarian Dunkler Weizenbock, Schalchner Weisser Bock, Penn Weizenbock; Pale - Weihenstephaner Vitus, Ayinger Weizenbock, Distelhauser Weizen Bock, Ladenburger Weizenbock Hell.

styles.name: Ordinary Bitter
text: Aroma: low-mod malt, often light caramel, bready/biscuity/lightly toasty; mild-mod fruitiness; hop aroma moderate to none (floral/earthy/resiny/fruity); generally no diacetyl (very low allowed). Flavor: medium to mod-high bitterness; mod-low to mod-high fruity esters; moderate-low hop flavor; low-medium maltiness, dry finish; optional low-mod caramel/toffee; often decidedly bitter. Mouthfeel: light to medium-light, low carbonation (bottled moderate).

Pale/amber/crystal malts, touch of dark malt for color, sugar/corn/wheat adjuncts possible; English finishing hops traditional (American hops with light touch); characterful British ale yeast. Lowest-gravity bitter.
Comparison: some all-pale versions are golden/summer ales; emphasis on bittering hops, not aggressive mid/late hopping like American ales.
Commercial: Fuller's Chiswick Bitter, Brains Bitter, Bateman's XB, Brakspear Gravity, Greene King IPA, Tetley's Original Bitter.

styles.name: Best Bitter
text: Aroma: low-mod malt, often low to med-low caramel, bready/biscuit/toasty; mild-mod fruitiness; hop aroma moderate to none; generally no diacetyl (very low allowed). Flavor: medium to mod-high bitterness; mod-low to mod-high esters; moderate-low earthy/resiny/fruity/floral hop flavor; low-medium malt, dry finish; optional low-mod caramel/toffee. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, low carbonation (bottled moderate).
Pale/amber/crystal malts, most contain sugar, touch of caramel/dark malt, corn/wheat possible; English finishing hops; British yeast.
Comparison: more malt flavor, alcohol and better ingredients than Ordinary; less alcohol than Strong Bitter; more caramel/base malt and color than British Golden Ale.
Commercial: Fuller's London Pride, Timothy Taylor Landlord, Adnams Southwold Bitter, Harvey's Sussex Best Bitter, Surrey Hills Shere Drop, Salopian Darwin's Origin.

styles.name: Strong Bitter
text: Aroma: hop aroma mod-high to mod-low (floral/earthy/resiny/fruity); medium to med-high malt aroma, optional low-mod caramel; med-low to med-high fruity esters; generally no diacetyl (very low allowed). Flavor: medium to med-high bitterness with supporting bready/biscuity/nutty/toasty malt, optional caramel/toffee; moderate to mod-high hop flavor; mod-low to high esters; optional low alcohol; medium-dry to dry finish; hops must not totally dominate malt. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium-full, low-moderate carbonation, slight alcohol warmth in stronger ones.
Pale/amber/crystal malts, touch of black for color, sugar/corn/wheat possible; English finishing hops; British yeast; Burton versions use medium-high sulfate water (dryness, minerally/sulfury note).

Comparison: more evident malt/hop flavors and alcohol than Best Bitter; overlaps British Strong Ales but paler and more bitter; more malt (caramel) and esters than American Pale Ale. "ESB" is a Fuller's trademark in the UK; US ESBs are malty, reddish, standard-strength.
Commercial: Bass Ale, Bateman's Triple XB, Robinsons Trooper, Samuel Smith's Organic Pale Ale, Shepherd Neame Bishop's Finger, Summit Extra Pale Ale.

styles.name: British Golden Ale
text: Aroma: hop mod-low to mod-high, any variety (English floral/herbal/earthy or American citrus; often single hop showcased); low bready malt, NO caramel; med-low to low fruitiness from hops rather than esters; low diacetyl optional. Flavor: medium to med-high bitterness; moderate to mod-high hop flavor (citrus increasingly common); med-low to low bready/slightly biscuity malt; caramel absent; mod-low to low esters; medium-dry to dry finish; low diacetyl optional. Mouthfeel: light to medium, low-moderate carbonation on draught; stronger versions slight warmth.

Low-color pale or lager malt as blank canvas; sugar/corn/wheat possible; English or American citrusy hops; somewhat clean British yeast. Served colder than bitters; golden bitter/summer ale/British blonde.
Comparison: closest to American Pale Ale but often lower ABV with British ingredients; no caramel and fewer esters than British Bitters; hoppiness between Blonde Ale and APA.
Commercial: Hop Back Summer Lightning, Fuller's/Spitfire Golden Ale (Shepherd Neame Spitfire Golden Ale), Adnams Explorer, Crouch Vale Brewers Gold, Oakham JHB, Golden Hill Exmoor Gold.

styles.name: Australian Sparkling Ale
text: Aroma: soft, clean, balanced esters/hops/malt/yeast at moderate to low intensity; esters pears/apples, maybe light banana; hops earthy/herbaceous or iron-like Pride of Ringwood note; malt neutral grainy to lightly bready, no caramel; fresh examples may be slightly yeasty/sulfury. Flavor: medium to low rounded grainy/bready malt, medium to med-high bitterness rising mid-palate; no caramel; highly attenuated dry crisp finish with lingering bitterness but impression of fullness; medium to med-high earthy/herbal/peppery/iron-like hop flavor (not floral); pear/apple esters; banana optional but never dominant; may be minerally/sulfury. Mouthfeel: high to very high carbonation (spritzy, carbonic bite), medium to medium-full body (fuller if poured with yeast); no residual sweetness.

Lightly kilned Australian 2-row (lager malt ok), crystal only for color, modern examples no adjuncts (cane sugar for priming only); Cluster/Goldings historically, Pride of Ringwood since mid-1960s; highly attenuative Burton-type (Australian) yeast; low carbonate/moderate sulfate water. Naturally carbonated, bottle-conditioned; yeast roused when poured gives cloudy look.
Comparison: like English Pale Ale but far more carbonated, less caramel, fewer late hops, showcases signature yeast/hop; more bitter than IBUs suggest.
Commercial: Coopers Sparkling Ale.

styles.name: English IPA
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-high hop (floral, spicy-peppery, citrus-orange); slight dry-hop ok; med-low to medium bready/biscuity malt, optional mod-low caramel/toasty; low-mod fruitiness; optional light sulfur. Flavor: medium to high hop flavor like aroma; moderate to assertive bitterness; medium-low to medium bready malt (biscuit, toast, toffee, caramel optional); med-low to medium fruitiness; medium-dry to very dry finish, bitterness may linger but not harsh; hop-leaning balance; high-sulfate water adds minerally dry finish and sulfur. Mouthfeel: smooth, med-light to medium, medium to med-high carbonation, no hop astringency; stronger ones warming.

Pale ale malt; English finishing hops; attenuative British ale yeast; refined sugar possible; optional Burton sulfate. Should NOT show oak or Brett despite cask shipping. Per CAMRA ~3.5% "IPAs" not true to style.
Comparison: more late hops, less fruitiness and caramel than British pale ales and Bitters; less hop intensity and more malt than American IPA.
Commercial: Worthington White Shield, Thornbridge Jaipur, Meantime London IPA, Fuller's Bengal Lancer, Marston's Old Empire, Berkshire Lost Sailor.

styles.name: Dark Mild
text: Aroma: low-mod malt, maybe fruitiness, wide malt expression (caramel, toffee, grainy, toasted, nutty, chocolate, light roast); low earthy/floral hop optional; very low diacetyl optional. Flavor: generally malty, wide range of malt/yeast flavors (caramel, toffee, toast, nutty, chocolate, coffee, roast, licorice, plum, raisin) on bready/biscuity/toasty base; sweet to dry finish; low to moderate bitterness; moderate fruity esters, low hop flavor, low diacetyl optional. Mouthfeel: light to medium, low to med-low carbonation, roasty versions slightly astringent; should not be flat, watery or thin.

Pale British base malts (dextrinous), crystal, dark malts or dark sugars, flaked maize possible, may use brewer's caramel; characterful British yeast; any hops (muted). Usually ~3.2% on cask; 4%+ versions for export/seasonal.
Comparison: some versions resemble lower-gravity modern English Porter; much less sweet than London Brown Ale.
Commercial: Moorhouse Black Cat, Theakston Traditional Mild, Greene King XX Mild, Hobson's Champion Mild, Mighty Oak Oscar Wilde, Brain's Dark.

styles.name: British Brown Ale
text: Aroma: light sweet malt with toffee, nutty, light chocolate, light to heavy caramel; light floral/earthy hop; light fruity not dominant. Flavor: gentle to moderate malt sweetness, light to heavy caramel, medium to dry finish; nutty/toasted/biscuity/toffee/light chocolate; medium to medium-low bitterness; even to malt-focused balance; low hop flavor and low-mod esters optional. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, medium to med-high carbonation.

British mild or pale ale malt with caramel malts, small amounts darker malts (chocolate) for color/nuttiness; English hops most authentic. No strongly roasted flavors. London Brown Ale (sweeter, 27 Historical) is a separate style.
Comparison: more malty balance and darker-grain flavor than British Bitters; stronger than Dark Mild; less roast than English Porter; stronger and much less sweet than London Brown Ale.
Commercial: Newcastle Brown Ale, Samuel Smith's Nut Brown Ale, Riggwelter Yorkshire Ale, AleSmith Nut Brown Ale, Cigar City Maduro Brown Ale, Maxim Double Maxim.

styles.name: English Porter
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-low bready/biscuity/toasty malt with mild roast often chocolate; caramel, nuts, toffee possible; up to moderate floral/earthy hops; moderate fruity esters optional but desirable; low diacetyl optional. Flavor: moderate bready/biscuity/toasty malt with mild-mod chocolate roastiness, often caramel/nutty/toffee, possibly coffee/licorice; not burnt or harshly roasted (small bitter-chocolate complexity ok); up to moderate earthy/floral hop; low-mod fruity esters; med-low to medium bitterness; fairly dry to slightly sweet finish; moderately-low diacetyl optional. Mouthfeel: med-light to medium, mod-low to mod-high carbonation, light-moderate creamy texture.
Dark-producing grist (chocolate/roasted malt, caramel malt, sugars); London-type often uses brown malt; British ale yeast. Called simply "Porter" in Britain. Historical re-creations go to Cat 27.
Comparison: softer, sweeter, more caramelly, lower gravity/ABV than American Porter (which is also hoppier); more substance and roast than British Brown Ale; higher gravity than Dark Mild.
Commercial: Fuller's London Porter, Samuel Smith Taddy Porter, Burton Bridge Burton Porter, Bateman's Salem Porter, RCH Old Slug Porter, Nethergate Old Growler Porter.

styles.name: Scottish Light
text: Aroma: low-med caramel/toffee, toasty-sugary (biscuit, graham cracker, butterscotch); light pome fruit and light English hops allowed.
Flavor: medium toasty-bready malt with caramel/toffee, slightly roasty dry finish; clean; bitterness just enough to avoid cloying.
Mouthfeel: med-low to medium body; low-mod carbonation; may be creamy.
Key: clean yeast, light esters OK, light English hop OK; no smoke/peat; pale malt + colour malt/sugar/corn/crystal; soft water. Usually draught, rare.
Comparison: darker and weaker than other Scottish ales; strength like low-end dark mild but different balance.
Examples: Belhaven Best, McEwan's 60.

styles.name: Scottish Heavy
text: Aroma: med-low to medium caramel/toffee, toasty-sugary; light pome fruit and English hop allowed.
Flavor: same profile as Light (toasty-bready, caramel/toffee, light roasty dry finish), clean.
Mouthfeel: med-low to medium body; low-mod carbonation; maybe creamy.
Key: clean fermentation; light esters/hops OK; no smoke; soft water.
Comparison: lighter colour and stronger than Light; similar strength to ordinary bitter, different balance.
Examples: McEwan's 70, Orkney Raven Ale.

styles.name: Scottish Export
text: Aroma: medium caramel/toffee, toasty-sugary; light pome fruit and English hop allowed.
Flavor: medium toasty-bready malt, caramel/toffee, slight roasty dry finish; clean.
Mouthfeel: medium body; med-low to medium carbonation; may be creamy.
Key: clean; light esters/hops OK; no smoke; Americanized versions often stronger.
Comparison: strongest of the three with same flavor profile; similar strength to best/strong bitter.
Examples: Belhaven Scottish Ale, Broughton Wee Jock 80 Shilling, Caledonian Edinburgh Castle, McEwan's 80/-, Orkney Dark Island, Traquair Bear Ale.

styles.name: Irish Red Ale
text: Aroma: low-mod neutral-grainy malt or light caramel/toast/toffee; very light buttery (diacetyl) optional; low earthy/floral hops optional; clean.

Flavor: little to moderate caramel sweetness, grainy-biscuity/toasty palate, light roasted-grain dryness in finish; med to med-low bitterness; medium-dry to dry finish; low esters optional; slightly malt-leaning.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body (slightly slick if low diacetyl); moderate carbonation; smooth.
Key: diacetyl optional (very light); esters low optional; hops earthy/floral light; pale base malt plus a bit of roasted barley/black malt for red colour and dry finish; caramel malt not always used.

Comparison: less bitter/hoppy Irish counterpart to English Bitter, drier from roasted barley; more attenuated, less caramel and body than equal-strength Scottish ales. Irish examples lower ABV/grainier/drier; non-Irish sweeter, stronger, estery.
Examples: Franciscan Well Rebel Red, Kilkenny Irish Beer, O'Hara's Irish Red, Murphy's Irish Red, Porterhouse Red, Smithwick's.

styles.name: Irish Stout
text: Aroma: moderate coffee dominant; slight dark chocolate/cocoa/roast; low-med esters optional; low earthy/floral hop optional.
Flavor: moderate roasted grain/malt, medium to high bitterness; dry coffee finish to slightly balanced with caramel/malt sweetness; bittersweet chocolate; medium earthy hop optional.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium-full, creamy esp. nitro; low-mod carbonation; light roast astringency OK, harshness not.
Key: pronounced roast; esters optional; pale malt + dark roasted grains/barley, unmalted grains for body; Dublin type drier/bitterer, Cork type sweeter/chocolatey. Bottled lacks nitro creaminess.
Comparison: lower strength than Irish Extra Stout; black vs brown English Porter.
Examples: Beamish Irish Stout, Belhaven Black Stout, Guinness Draught, Murphy's Irish Stout, O'Hara's Irish Stout, Porterhouse Irish Stout.

styles.name: Irish Extra Stout
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-high coffee, with dark chocolate/cocoa/biscuit/vanilla; low-med esters optional; hops low to none.

Flavor: moderate to mod-high dark roast, medium to med-high bitterness; dry coffee to moderately balanced with up to moderate sweetness; dark chocolate, mocha/biscuit background; low fruitiness optional; earthy/spicy hop optional.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, creamy; moderate carbonation; very smooth; slight warming possible; light roast astringency OK.
Key: like Irish Stout but stronger/richer; may add dark crystal malts or dark sugars; traditionally bottled; traditional Irish commercial examples ~5.6-6.0%.
Comparison: midway between Irish Stout and Foreign Extra Stout in strength; more body/richness/malt complexity than Irish Stout; black not brown.
Examples: Guinness Extra Stout, O'Hara's Leann Follain, Porterhouse XXXX, Sheaf Stout.

styles.name: Sweet Stout
text: Aroma: mild roasted grain, coffee/chocolate; cream-like sweetness; fruitiness low to mod-high; low diacetyl optional; low floral/earthy hop optional.

Flavor: roasted coffee/chocolate dominate; low-mod fruity esters; moderate bitterness; medium to high sweetness lasting into finish (quite sweet to moderately dry); low diacetyl optional; low hop optional.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, creamy; low-mod carbonation; high residual sweetness.

Key: lactose commonly added (unfermentable sweetness; "milk/cream stout" names no longer legal in England); pale malt + dark malts/grains; adjuncts OK; mild not burnt roast; early 1900s invalid/tonic stout.
Comparison: much sweeter, less bitter than other stouts (except Tropical); roast mild not burnt; like Oatmeal Stout but sweeter.
Examples: Bristol Beer Factory Milk Stout, Firestone Nitro Merlin Milk Stout, Left Hand Milk Stout, Lancaster Milk Stout, Mackeson's XXX Stout, Marston's Oyster Stout.

styles.name: Oatmeal Stout
text: Aroma: mild grainy roasty coffee with light malty sweetness (coffee-and-cream); fruitiness low to med-high; med-low earthy/floral hop optional; light nutty oat optional; med-low diacetyl optional but typically absent.

Flavor: mild roasted coffee/milk chocolate, low to mod-high fruit; oats toasty/nutty/grainy; medium bitterness; medium-sweet to medium-dry finish; malty-roasty-nutty aftertaste; hop flavor med-low optional; diacetyl typically absent.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, smooth/silky/velvety, sometimes oily from oats; creamy; medium to med-high carbonation; stronger may warm.

Key: noticeable oats (5-20%+ oatmeal or malted oats), not symbolic; pale/caramel/chocolate malts and roasted grains; hops mainly bittering; English ale yeast; American versions hoppier, less sweet, less fruity.
Comparison: cross between Irish Extra Stout and Sweet Stout with oats; sweeter ones like Sweet Stout with oats instead of lactose, drier like a nuttier Irish Extra Stout; emphasises body/mouthfeel.
Examples: Anderson Valley Barney Flats, St-Ambroise Oatmeal Stout, Samuel Smith Oatmeal Stout, Broughton Stout Jock, Summit Oatmeal Stout, Young's London Stout.

styles.name: Tropical Stout
text: Aroma: moderate-high sweetness prominent; mod-high coffee/chocolate roast (not burnt); medium-high fruitiness; molasses, licorice, burnt sugar, dried fruit, vinous; clean alcohol in stronger; low hop and low diacetyl optional.

Flavor: quite sweet with smooth dark grain; restrained med-low to medium bitterness; smooth roast (coffee/chocolate) moderated by sweet finish; no burnt/harsh bite; mod-high fruity esters; dark rum/molasses/burnt sugar; low hop optional; med-low diacetyl optional.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, smooth creamy; warming not hot; moderate to mod-high carbonation.
Key: scaled-up sweet stout; "tropical" refers to origin/market, not tropical-fruit hops; adjuncts/sugar to boost gravity; typically warm-fermented lager yeast; hops for bittering only.

Comparison: scaled-up Sweet Stout with more fruit; like some Imperial Stouts but without bitterness/burnt roast/late hops and lower ABV; far sweeter, less hoppy than American Stout; sweeter and less bitter than same-gravity Foreign Extra Stout.
Examples: ABC Extra Stout, Bahamian Strong Back Stout, Dragon Stout, Jamaica Stout, Lion Stout, Royal Extra Stout.

styles.name: Foreign Extra Stout
text: Aroma: moderate-high roast (coffee, dark chocolate, lightly burnt grain); low-med fruit; may be sweet, molasses, licorice, dried fruit, vinous; subtle clean alcohol; low earthy/herbal/floral hop optional; low diacetyl optional.
Flavor: moderate-high roast without sharp bite; low-med esters; medium to high bitterness; moderately dry finish; moderate earthy/herbal/floral hop optional; med-low diacetyl optional.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, smooth/sometimes creamy; warming not hot; moderate to mod-high carbonation.

Key: strong export stout (heavier hopped, longer shelf life; historic long maturation maybe with Brett); pale + dark roasted malts/grains, historically brown/amber malt; typically English hops for bittering; adjuncts/sugar OK. Also called Foreign/Export Stout.
Comparison: like Irish Extra Stout balance but more alcohol; smaller than Imperial Stout; lacks American Stout's strong bitterness and late hops; same gravity as Tropical but drier and more bitter.
Examples: Coopers Best Extra Stout, Guinness Foreign Extra Stout, The Kernel Export Stout London 1890, La Cumbre Malpais, Pelican Tsunami Export, Ridgeway Foreign Export, Southwark Old Stout.

styles.name: British Strong Ale
text: Aroma: malty-sweet with fruity esters; dried fruit, caramel, nuts, toffee; some alcohol OK but not hot/solventy; hops vary (earthy, resiny, fruity, floral).

Flavor: medium-high rich malt (nutty, toffee, caramel; light chocolate in darker); sugar complexity; malty but may be well hopped; moderate fruity esters, dark/dried fruit; finish medium-dry to somewhat sweet; alcohol evident not overwhelming; low diacetyl optional but generally undesirable.
Mouthfeel: medium to full, chewy; alcohol warmth welcome; low-mod carbonation; smooth.

Key: an entry category more than a style (pale malty-hoppy, winter warmers, strong dark milds, small Burton ales); no aged character required; pale malt base with caramel/specialty malts, light dark malt; sugar/maize/flaked barley/wheat adjuncts common; English finishing hops; traditionally bottle-conditioned and cellared.

Comparison: overlaps Old Ale gravity but not aged; less rich/strong than English Barleywine; stronger than Strong Bitter, Brown Ale, Porter; more specialty malt/sugar character than American Strong Ale.
Examples: Fuller's 1845, Harvey's Elizabethan Ale, J.W. Lees Moonraker, McEwan's Champion, Samuel Smith's Winter Welcome, Shepherd Neame 1698.

styles.name: Old Ale
text: Aroma: malty-sweet, fruity esters; dried fruit, vinous, caramel, molasses, toffee, treacle; some alcohol and nutty oxidative notes (Sherry/Port/Madeira) OK; hop aroma not usually present.

Flavor: medium-high luscious malt (nut, caramel, molasses); light chocolate/roast optional, never prominent; malty-sweet but may be well hopped (bitterness perception falls with age); moderate-high fruity esters, dried-fruit/vinous; finish dry to somewhat sweet; oxidative sherry/port notes with aging OK; alcohol evident; low diacetyl optional.
Mouthfeel: medium to full, chewy (older may be thinner from continued attenuation); alcohol warmth welcome; low-mod carbonation; light acidity and wood tannin optional.

Key: defining quality is impression of age (oxidation, leather, vinous): normally faults but acceptable if pleasant and complex, never undrinkable; handling more than brewing; stock/stale ale heritage; composition like British Strong Ale. Old Peculier is unique.
Comparison: overlaps British Strong Ale and low-end English Barleywine but always aged; split from Barleywine above 7% ABV is arbitrary, defined by greater age.
Examples: Avery Old Jubilation, Berlina Old Ale, Burton Bridge Olde Expensive, Gale's Prize Old Ale, Greene King Strong Suffolk Ale, Marston Owd Roger, Theakston Old Peculier.

styles.name: Wee Heavy
text: Aroma: strong bready-toasty malt, high caramel/toffee (breadcrumbs, biscuits, nougat, butterscotch); faint roast sometimes; low-mod dark/dried fruit esters and alcohol; very low earthy/floral/citrus/spicy hops optional.

Flavor: rich, bready-toasty, often full and sweet, caramel/toffee, balanced by alcohol and hint of grainy roast in finish; medium-low alcohol and esters (plum, raisin); low bitterness; sweet to medium-dry finish; med-low hop flavor optional.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full, thick/chewy, sometimes creamy; smooth alcohol warmth desirable; moderate carbonation.

Key: Scottish pale ale malt, adjuncts OK, crystal or darker grains for colour; NO peat smoke; range of strengths (a ~5% variant and a ~8-9% variant); aka Strong Scotch Ale; descended from Edinburgh ales.
Comparison: somewhat like English Barleywine but often darker and more caramelly.
Examples: Belhaven Wee Heavy, Broughton Old Jock, Gordon Highland Scotch Ale, Inveralmond Blackfriar, McEwan's Scotch Ale, Orkney Skull Splitter, Traquair House Ale, Duck-Rabbit Wee Heavy.

styles.name: English Barleywine
text: Aroma: very rich, strongly malty (caramel in darker, light toffee in paler; bready/toasty); moderate-strong fruit, dark/dried fruit; hops mild to assertive (floral, earthy, tea, marmalade); soft rounded alcohol; sherry/port notes with age.

Flavor: medium-high rich malty sweetness, complex bread/biscuit/caramel (toffee in pale); medium-high fruitiness; hop flavor/bitterness vary widely (English character), bitterness fades with age; finish moderately dry to moderately sweet; some oxidative/vinous flavors with age OK at noticeable-not-prominent level; pale versions more bitter, attenuated, hoppy.
Mouthfeel: full, chewy, velvety; smooth non-burning warmth; low-mod carbonation.
Key: golden amber to dark brown, not black/opaque; British pale and crystal malts, limited dark malts, brewing sugars, English hops, British yeast; changes with age; "Barley Wine" is UK spelling.
Comparison: less hoppy/bitter, maltier, fruitier than American Barleywine; overlaps low-end Old Ale without heavy age; less caramelly and often less sweet than Wee Heavy.
Examples: Burton Bridge Thomas Sykes Old Ale, Coniston No. 9, Fuller's Golden Pride, Hogs Back A over T, J.W. Lee's Vintage Harvest Ale, Robinson's Old Tom.

styles.name: Blonde Ale
text: Aroma: light-mod neutral/grainy malt, maybe bread/caramel; low-mod fruitiness optional; low-med hop (any variety; citrus/floral/fruity/spicy common); clean fermentation.

Flavor: soft initial maltiness, light character malt (bread, toast, biscuit, wheat); caramel usually absent (if any, low-colour/honey); low-med fruity esters optional; light-mod hop flavor, not aggressive; med-low to medium bitterness; balance malt-leaning to even; finish medium-dry to slightly malty; clean.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body; medium to high carbonation; smooth, not heavy.

Key: generally all-malt, may include wheat/sugar; any hop; clean American, lightly fruity English or Kolsch yeast; lager yeast/cold-conditioned possible (any fermentation). Oxidation can give honey/caramel notes (not malt-derived). aka Golden Ale.
Comparison: more flavor than American Lager/Cream Ale; less bitter than APA; similar to maltier Kolsch.
Examples: Firestone Walker 805, Kona Big Wave Golden Ale, Real Ale Fireman's #4, Russian River Aud Blonde, Victory Summer Love, Widmer Citra Summer Blonde.

styles.name: American Pale Ale
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-high American/New World hops (citrus, floral, pine, resin, spice, tropical/stone fruit, berry, melon; none required); low-mod neutral/grainy malt, low specialty malt (bread, toast, biscuit, caramel); fruity esters optional up to moderate; fresh dry-hop optional.

Flavor: hop/malt like aroma; caramel absent or restrained; moderate to high bitterness; clean fermentation; esters moderate to none; medium to dry finish; late-hop/bitterness-leaning balance, malt supportive; clean aftertaste.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium; moderate-high carbonation; smooth, no harshness.
Key: neutral pale malt, small specialty malts, American/New World hops, neutral to lightly fruity American or English ale yeast; allow for new hop varieties; often like lower-gravity IPAs.

Comparison: lighter, cleaner, less caramel than English pale ale; overlaps American Amber in colour but cleaner, less caramel, lighter body, more finishing hops; less bitter/strong than American IPA; maltier/more balanced than Session IPA; hoppier/more bitter than Blonde.
Examples: Deschutes Mirror Pond, Half Acre Daisy Cutter, Great Lakes Burning River, La Cumbre Acclimated APA, Sierra Nevada Pale Ale, Stone Pale Ale 2.0.

styles.name: American Amber Ale
text: Aroma: low-mod American/New World hops (citrus common); mod-low to mod-high malt, usually moderate caramel that may support, balance or mask hops; esters moderate to none.

Flavor: moderate-high hop flavor; moderate-strong malt: initial sweetness then moderate caramel, minor toasty/biscuity; no dark/roasted malt; moderate to mod-high bitterness; balance somewhat malty to somewhat bitter; esters moderate to none; medium-to-full yet dry finish.
Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full; medium-high carbonation; smooth; slight warmth in stronger ones.

Key: neutral pale ale malt with medium-dark crystal; American/New World (often citrusy) hops; neutral to lightly estery yeast; hoppy versions must not clash with caramel; progenitor of Red IPA/Double Red.

Comparison: darker, more caramel, more body, less bitter than APA; less alcohol/bitterness/hop than Red IPA; less strength/malt/hop than American Strong Ale; less chocolate/dark caramel than American Brown.
Examples: Anderson Valley Boont Amber, Bell's Amber, Full Sail Amber, North Coast Red Seal, Saint Arnold Amber, Troegs Hopback Amber.

styles.name: California Common
text: Aroma: moderate-high herbal/resinous/floral/minty hops; light fruitiness OK; low-mod caramel or toasty malt.

Flavor: moderately malty, pronounced hop bitterness; toast (not roast) and caramel; low to mod-high rustic traditional American hop flavor (herbal, resinous, floral, minty); dry crisp finish with lingering bitterness and firm grainy malt; light fruity esters OK, otherwise clean.
Mouthfeel: medium body; medium to med-high carbonation.

Key: narrowly defined around Anchor Steam; Northern Brewer-type non-citrusy traditional hops (modern citrusy New World hops inappropriate); pale ale malt, small toasted/crystal malt; LAGER yeast fermented warm (55-60 F), California-type strains preferred (some German strains give inappropriate sulfur); historic open shallow coolship fermentation.

Comparison: superficially like American Amber but toastier malt, always assertive traditional-hop bitterness, warm-fermented lager yeast; less attenuated/carbonated/fruity than Australian Sparkling Ale.
Examples: Anchor Steam, Steamworks Steam Engine Lager.

styles.name: American Brown Ale
text: Aroma: moderate malty-sweet to rich, chocolate/caramel/nutty/toasty; hops low-mod, nearly any type that complements malt (stronger/American hop/dry-hop interpretations optional); esters moderate to very low; dark malt more robust than other browns but not Porter-like.

Flavor: medium to mod-high malty with chocolate/caramel/nutty/toasty; medium to med-high bitterness; medium to medium-dry finish with malt and hop aftertaste; light-mod hop flavor (maybe citrusy/fruity/tropical); esters very low to moderate; malt and hops about equal; no roasty Porter/Stout character.
Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full; resiny dry impression in more bitter ones; moderate to mod-high carbonation; stronger may warm.

Key: pale malt + crystal and chocolate; American hops typical (continental/New World OK); reflects current commercial examples, not early hoppier/stronger homebrew; IPA-strength versions go to 21B Brown IPA.

Comparison: more chocolate/caramel than APA/Amber, usually less bitter in balance; less bitter/alcoholic/hoppy than Brown IPA; more bitter, hoppier than English Brown, richer malt, higher alcohol, American hop character.
Examples: Avery Ellie's Brown, Big Sky Moose Drool, Brooklyn Brown, Bell's Best Brown, Smuttynose Old Brown Dog, Telluride Face Down Brown.

styles.name: American Porter
text: Aroma: med-light to med-strong roast, often chocolate, light coffee or lightly burnt; background caramel/toffee or malty richness; resiny/earthy/floral hops low to high; moderate fruity esters optional; never sharp/acrid/acidic; always some roast aroma.

Flavor: moderately strong roast (chocolate, lightly burnt), sometimes caramel/malty richness; medium to high bitterness; dry to medium-sweet finish; low to high resiny/earthy/floral hop flavor that must not clash (dry-hopped versions may be resiny/fresh); moderate esters optional; no acidic bite or acrid/harsh burnt character.
Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full; mod-low to mod-high carbonation; stronger may warm; slight dark-malt astringency OK, not strong.

Key: also "Robust Porter"; broad style open to interpretation (hoppy or not; American or British feel); pale base, frequent crystal, black/chocolate malts; American bittering hops, US or UK finishing; clean US or characterful English ale yeast.
Comparison: more bitter, often stronger, more dark-malt character and dryness than English Porter or Pre-Prohibition Porter; less strong/assertive than American Stout.
Examples: Anchor Porter, Bell's Porter, Deschutes Black Butte, Great Lakes Edmund Fitzgerald, Sierra Nevada Porter, Smuttynose Robust Porter.

styles.name: American Stout
text: Aroma: moderate-strong roast (roasted coffee, dark chocolate); burnt/charcoal acceptable at low levels; hop aroma medium to very low, citrusy/resiny; medium esters optional; light alcohol optional; never sharp/acrid/acidic.

Flavor: moderate to very high roast (coffee, dark/bittersweet chocolate, roasted beans; slightly burnt grounds not prominent); low-med malt sweetness with chocolate/caramel; medium to high bitterness; low to high citrusy/resiny hop flavor; medium to dry finish, occasionally lightly burnt; low esters optional; light smooth alcohol optional.
Mouthfeel: medium to full, can be creamy; roast astringency OK if not excessive; med-high to high carbonation; light to moderately strong smooth warmth.

Key: jet black, usually opaque; common American base malts/yeast/hops; varied dark/roasted and caramel malts; low-level adjuncts allowed; once called "West Coast Stout"; aggressive American hopping on a strong English/Irish stout.

Comparison: like a hoppy, bitter, strongly roasted Irish Extra Stout; much more roast and body than Black IPA; bigger/stronger goes to Imperial Stout; stronger and more assertive (dark malt and hops) than American Porter.
Examples: Avery Out of Bounds Stout, Deschutes Obsidian Stout, Sierra Nevada Stout, Bell's Kalamazoo Stout, Trillium Secret Stairs.

styles.name: Imperial Stout
text: Aroma: rich, deep, complex, often intense blend of roast, fruit, hops, alcohol; roast from coffee/bittersweet chocolate/cocoa/licorice/tar/slightly burnt; dark/dried fruit esters (plum, prune, fig, currant, raisin); hops very low to aggressive, English or American; alcohol optional but not sharp/hot/solventy; age adds vinous/port notes, never sourness.

Flavor: same four components, often more intense than aroma; medium to aggressively high bitterness; maltiness (bread, toast, caramel) supports; dry to moderately sweet finish (changes with age); must not be syrupy/cloying; roast-bitterness-warmth aftertaste.
Mouthfeel: full to very full, chewy, velvety; background smooth warmth; low-mod carbonation; body may decline with age.

Key: very dark reddish-brown to jet black, opaque; also "Russian Imperial Stout"/RIS; American versions more bitter/roasty/late-hopped, English more specialty-malt and estery, anything between allowed (don't judge as clones); pale malt + significant roasted malt/grain, flaked adjuncts common; American or English ale yeast and hops; ages well; base for many specialty beers.
Comparison: darker and more roasty than Barleywines with similar alcohol; more complex, wider flavor range than lower-gravity stouts.

Examples: American: Bell's Expedition Stout, Great Divide Yeti, North Coast Old Rasputin, Oskar Blues Ten Fidy, Sierra Nevada Narwhal. English: Thornbridge Saint Petersburg, Courage Imperial Russian Stout, Le Coq Imperial Extra Double Stout, Samuel Smith Imperial Stout, 2SP The Russian.

styles.name: American IPA
text: Aroma: prominent to intense American/New World hops (citrus, floral, pine, resin, spice, tropical/stone fruit, berry, melon); low to med-low clean grainy malt; generally clean fermentation, light fruitiness OK; restrained alcohol optional.

Flavor: medium to very high hop flavor; low to med-low clean grainy malt, maybe light caramel/toast; med-high to very high bitterness; dry to medium-dry finish; hoppy bitter aftertaste; low esters optional; clean alcohol background optional.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body; smooth; medium to med-high carbonation; no harshness.

Key: oak inappropriate (goes to 33A); clear but light haze allowed; pale base malt, American or English yeast clean/slightly fruity; generally all-malt, sugar acceptable; restrained crystal; any hops OK (new varieties allowed). IPL can enter here if similar. "West Coast IPA" = dry, sharply bitter, clear type of 21A.

Comparison: stronger and hoppier than APA; vs English IPA: less caramel/bread/toast, more American/New World hops, fewer esters, less body, hoppier balance, slightly stronger; less alcohol than Double IPA but similar balance.
Examples: Bell's Two-Hearted, Cigar City Jai Alai, Fat Heads Head Hunter, Firestone Walker Union Jack, Maine Lunch, Russian River Blind Pig.

styles.name: Specialty IPA
text: Category note: not a distinct style; IPA balance (hop-forward, bitter, dryish) plus a minor tweak; entrant must declare strength (session ABV 3.0-5.0%, standard 5.0-7.5%, double 7.5-10.0%; default standard) and type (or describe it). Not for classic IPAs with added fruit/spice/wood/smoke (those go to specialty-type categories). Session IPA = 21B with 21A base at session strength; Double IPA is 22A not 21B. Hop aroma required; harshness, heaviness, hop/specialty-ingredient clashes are faults.
Generic: hop flavor med-low to high; bitterness med-high to very high; malt low to medium; medium-dry to dry finish; smooth, med-light to medium body; medium carbonation.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Belgian IPA
text: Aroma: moderate-high American/New World (tropical, melon, stone fruit, citrus, pine) or continental (spicy, herbal, floral) hops, maybe dry-hop; gentle sugary/honey malt, rarely caramel; moderate-high esters (pear, apple, citrus, banana); light clove/pepper optional; light alcohol optional.

Flavor: moderate fruity and spicy yeast flavors; moderate-high hop flavor; light neutral grainy malt (low toast/caramel/honey optional); moderate-high bitterness; dry to medium-dry finish accentuating bitterness; lingering non-harsh bitterness.
Mouthfeel: light to medium body; medium to high carbonation (lightens body); light warmth optional.

Key: Belgian Tripel/Golden Strong yeast + IPA hopping; yeast and hop choice critical (many clash); US versions use American/New World hops, Belgian ones European hops with only pale malt; sugar adjuncts common; dates from mid-2000s.
Comparison: cross of American/Double IPA with Belgian Golden Strong or Tripel; spicier, stronger, drier, fruitier than American IPA.
Examples: Brewery Vivant Triomphe, Houblon Chouffe, Green Flash Le Freak, Urthel Hop It.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Black IPA
text: Aroma: moderate-high hops (stone fruit, tropical, citrus, resin, pine, berry, melon); very low to moderate malt with possible light chocolate/coffee/toast and background caramel; clean fermentation, light esters OK.

Flavor: med-low to high hop flavor; low-med malt with restrained chocolate/coffee, not burnt/ashy and not clashing with hops; light caramel/toffee optional; med-high to very high bitterness; dry to slightly off-dry finish, bitter but not harsh, light roast adds dryness; low-mod esters optional.
Mouthfeel: smooth; med-light to medium body; medium carbonation; light creaminess optional.

Key: dark brown to black, light haze OK but not murky; DEBITTERED roast malts (Schwarzbier-type restrained roast); any American/New World hop; most are standard strength; strong ones can become hoppy porters; origin Greg Noonan ~1990.
Comparison: IPA/Double IPA balance with restrained roast; less rich/roasty than American Stout/Porter, less body, smoother, more drinkable.
Examples: 21st Amendment Back in Black, Duck-Rabbit Hoppy Bunny ABA, Stone Sublimely Self-Righteous.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Brown IPA
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-high hops (stone/tropical fruit, citrus, resin, pine, berry, melon); med-low to medium malty-sweet (milk chocolate, cocoa, toffee, nuts, biscuit, dark caramel, toasted bread, dark fruit); clean; light esters/alcohol optional.

Flavor: medium to high hop flavor; med-low to medium supportive malt; no hop/malt clashes; med-high to high bitterness, no harshness; dry to medium finish, bitter-hoppy-malty aftertaste; no highly roasted/burnt malt; malt should nearly balance hops.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body; smooth; medium to med-high carbonation; light warmth optional.

Key: reddish-brown to dark brown, not black; medium/dark crystal, lightly roasted chocolate-type malts, intermediate colour malts; sugar incl. brown sugar OK; any American/New World hop that doesn't clash.
Comparison: stronger, more bitter American Brown with American IPA dryness; less roast than Black IPA, more chocolate than Red IPA.
Examples: Dogfish Head Indian Brown Ale, Harpoon Brown IPA, Russian River Janet's Brown Ale.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Brut IPA
text: Aroma: moderately high to intense bright hops (tropical, stone fruit, citrus, white grape; NOT grassy/vegetal/herbal); subtle neutral malt, never caramelly or corny-sweet; light clean alcohol optional; very clean fermentation, not yeasty.

Flavor: high to very high hop flavor; low to very low neutral malt, no caramel; perceived bitterness low to very low (bone-dry, very high carbonation); neutral to slightly fruity fermentation; NO diacetyl; dry to very dry finish, fresh hoppy aftertaste, clean bitterness.
Mouthfeel: light to very light body; spritzy high to very high carbonation (sparkling-wine-like); no hop astringency; alcohol warmth never hot.

Key: very pale straw to light gold, crystal clear (touch of haze OK), massive rocky white head; pilsner/very pale malt with up to 40% adjuncts; no crystal malt or lactose; enzymes (amyloglucosidase) for very low FG (misuse can cause diacetyl = flaw); oil-heavy modern hops via late/post-boil hopping; neutral yeast; origin 2017 San Francisco.

Comparison: less malt, bitterness and colour than American IPA, much drier and more carbonated; aroma/flavor like Hazy IPA but dry with little haze; pale/dry/carbonated like Belgian Golden Strong but weaker and no Belgian yeast.
Examples: Drake's Brightside Extra Brut IPA, Fair State The Brut Squad, Ommegang Brut IPA.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Red IPA
text: Aroma: moderate-strong hops (stone/tropical fruit, citrus, resin, pine, berry, melon); med-low to medium malty-sweet (medium-dark caramel, toffee, toasted bread, dark fruit); clean; light esters/alcohol optional.

Flavor: medium to very high hop flavor; med-low to medium supportive malt; no clashes; med-high to very high bitterness, no harshness; dry to medium finish, bitter-hoppy-malty aftertaste; malt must not overshadow hops.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body; smooth; medium to med-high carbonation; light warmth optional.
Key: light reddish-amber to dark reddish-copper, clear; IPA grist plus medium/dark crystal, some light-toasty character malts; sugar OK; any American/New World hop.
Comparison: stronger, hoppier, more bitter American Amber; less malty/sweet than American Strong Ale; drier, lower alcohol, less malty than American Barleywine; less chocolate/caramel than Brown IPA.
Examples: Avery Hog Heaven, Cigar City Tocobaga Red IPA, Modern Times Blazing World, Troegs Nugget Nectar.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: Rye IPA
text: Aroma: prominent to intense hops (stone/tropical fruit, citrus, resin, pine, berry, melon); low peppery rye aroma with clean grainy malt; clean fermentation; light esters/alcohol optional.

Flavor: medium to very high hop flavor; low to med-low supportive malt (light caramel/toast possible); low-moderate grainy, peppery, spicy rye adding to dry finish; med-high to very high bitterness, no harshness; dry bitter hoppy aftertaste.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body; smooth, maybe lightly creamy; medium to med-high carbonation.
Key: rye malt character must be noticeable (else 21A); generous rye malt; any American/New World hop; NO caraway, NO oak.
Comparison: drier, slightly spicier and creamier than American IPA with lingering bitterness/spice; lacks Roggenbier's intense rye or Weizen yeast character.
Examples: Founders Reds Rye, Sierra Nevada Ruthless Rye.

styles.name: Specialty IPA: White IPA
text: Aroma: moderate esters (orange, grapefruit, apricot, sometimes banana); light spices optional (coriander, orange peel, pepper, clove); med-low to medium hop (stone fruit, citrus, tropical); esters/spice may mask hops; low neutral/grainy/bready malt; light alcohol optional.
Flavor: moderate-high esters, med-low to med-high hop flavor, light spices; light bready malt; high bitterness; moderately dry refreshing finish.
Mouthfeel: medium-light body; medium to med-high carbonation; light spice astringency optional.

Key: pale to deep gold, typically hazy; pale and wheat malts, Belgian Witbier yeast, citrusy American hops; coriander and orange peel optional (spice impression from yeast, additions or both); craft cross of IPA and Witbier.
Comparison: bitter, hoppy, stronger like American IPA but fruity, spicy, light like Witbier; late hops usually less prominent than American IPA.
Examples: Lagunitas A Little Sumpin' Sumpin' Ale, New Belgium Accumulation.

styles.name: Hazy IPA
text: Aroma: intense fruity hops (stone fruit, tropical, citrus; not grassy/herbal); clean/neutral/lightly bready malt background, no caramel or toast (absent malt is a fault); neutral to fruity fermentation; yeast and hop esters must not clash; creamy/buttery/acidic aroma inappropriate; light alcohol optional.

Flavor: high to very high fruity hop flavor; low-medium malt; low to med-high perceived bitterness, masked by fuller body and soft off-dry to medium finish; non-sharp hop aftertaste; shouldn't be sweet (esters + low bitterness can suggest it); alcohol background optional.
Mouthfeel: medium to medium-full body; medium carbonation; smooth, maybe silky; no harshness; not thick/creamy/viscous, no acidic twang, no raw-starch texture.

Key: aka New England IPA / NEIPA; straw to light amber, hazy to opaque but "shine" not murky (floating hop matter/yeast clumps are faults); haze from polyphenol-protein interaction of dry-hopping, not yeast/starch; more flaked grains, little caramel/specialty malt; fruity American/New World hops; neutral to estery yeast; balanced to chloride-rich water; heavy dry hopping incl. during active fermentation (biotransformation); milkshake/smoothie-like examples out of style; added fruit/lactose/vanilla go to specialty categories.
Comparison: fuller, softer, more fruit-forward late hops, more restrained bitterness, hazier than American IPA; dry, crisp, at-most-medium-body, high-bitterness examples go in 21A.
Examples: Belching Beaver Hazers Gonna Haze, Hill Farmstead Susan, Other Half Green Diamonds, Pinthouse Electric Jellyfish, Tree House Julius, Trillium Congress Street, WeldWerks Juicy Bits.

styles.name: Double IPA
text: Aroma: prominent to intense modern American/New World hops (citrus, floral, pine, resin, spice, tropical/stone fruit, berry, melon); supportive clean neutral-grainy malt; neutral to lightly fruity fermentation; alcohol may show, not solventy.

Flavor: strong, complex hop flavor; mod-high to very high bitterness, not harsh; low-med soft malt (light caramel/toast OK); dry to medium-dry finish, not sweet/heavy, lingering hoppy bitter aftertaste; low-mod fruitiness optional; light clean alcohol OK.
Mouthfeel: med-light to medium body, smooth; medium to med-high carbonation; restrained alcohol warmth OK; no hop astringency.

Key: rarely "Imperial IPA"; neutral base malt, sugar adjuncts common, crystal rare; American/New World hops; neutral/lightly fruity yeast; NO oak; often multiple dry-hop additions; drinkability matters.
Comparison: bigger than English/American IPA in alcohol, bitterness, hoppiness; less malty-rich, lighter body, drier, more hop-dominant than American Barleywine.
Examples: Columbus Bodhi, Fat Heads Hop Juju, Port Brewing Hop 15, Russian River Pliny the Elder, Stone Ruination Double IPA 2.0, Wicked Weed Freak of Nature.

styles.name: American Strong Ale
text: Aroma: medium-high American/New World hops (citrus, floral, pine, resin, spice, tropical/stone fruit, berry, melon); moderate-bold malt, medium-dark caramel common, toasty/bready possible, background light roast/chocolate allowed; neutral to moderately fruity; alcohol may show, not solventy.

Flavor: medium-high malt (caramel, toffee, dark fruit; toasty/bready/rich complexity); light chocolate/roast allowed, not burnt/sharp; med-high to high bitterness; moderate-high hop flavor; low-mod esters; noticeable non-sharp alcohol OK; medium-high malty sweetness, finish somewhat dry to somewhat sweet, not syrupy/cloying; bitter-to-bittersweet aftertaste.
Mouthfeel: medium to full body; alcohol warmth OK, not excessively hot; light hop astringency allowed; med-low to medium carbonation.

Key: a grouping by balance rather than a style (modern Double Reds, strong malty-hoppy beers not quite Barleywine); medium amber to light brown; pale base, medium-dark crystal common; American/New World hops; neutral/lightly fruity yeast; kin to historic American stock ales without age character.
Comparison: not as strong/rich as American Barleywine; more malt-balanced than American/Double IPA; more American hop intensity than British Strong Ale; maltier and fuller than Red IPA.
Examples: Fat Head's Bone Head, Great Lakes Nosferatu, Oskar Blues G'Knight, Port Brewing Shark Attack Double Red, Stone Arrogant Bastard.

styles.name: American Barleywine
text: Aroma: strong malt and hop aroma dominate; hops moderate to assertive (American, New World or English; citrusy, fruity, resiny classic); strong grainy/bready/toasty/light caramel or neutral malt richness, typically not dark caramel/roast/deep fruit; low to moderately strong esters and alcohol (below malt and hops); intensities fade with age.

Flavor: similar to aroma; moderately strong to aggressive bitterness tempered by rich malt; moderate-high hop flavor; low-mod esters; noticeable non-solventy alcohol; mod-low to mod-high malty sweetness, somewhat malty to dry but full finish; age dries and smooths; malty balance but always bitter.
Mouthfeel: full, chewy, velvety; smooth non-burning alcohol warmth; low to moderate carbonation.

Key: amber to medium copper (rarely light brown), ruby highlights; pale malt + some specialty, dark malts used very sparingly; American hops typical (many varieties OK); American or English ale yeast; often seasonal/vintage; some now barrel-aged or rebranded as IPA.

Comparison: more hop bitterness/flavor/aroma than English Barley Wine; typically paler than dark English and darker than golden English versions, without deeper malt flavors; unlike Double IPA, hops not extreme, malt forward, fuller richer body, more residual sweetness (sipping vs drinking).
Examples: Anchor Old Foghorn, Bell's Third Coast Old Ale, East End Gratitude, Hair of the Dog Doggie Claws, Sierra Nevada Bigfoot.

styles.name: Wheatwine
text: Aroma: mild hops (any variety); moderate to mod-strong bready wheaty malt, often honey/caramel complexity; light clean alcohol; low-med fruity notes; very low diacetyl optional; banana-clove Weizen yeast character INAPPROPRIATE.

Flavor: moderate to mod-high bready wheat malt dominates over hops; low-mod toasty/caramel/biscuity/honey notes optional; low-med hop flavor (any variety); moderate to mod-high fruitiness, often dried fruit; low to moderate bitterness; malty to even balance; not syrupy or under-attenuated.
Mouthfeel: medium-full to full; chewy, luscious, velvety; low to moderate carbonation; light-moderate smooth warmth optional.

Key: gold to deep amber with garnet/ruby; chill haze allowed; typically American two-row + American wheat, usually 50%+ wheat malt; restrained dark malts; any hops; may be oak-aged; color partly from long boil; roots in American Wheat Beer, no Weizen yeast; first brewed Rubicon 1988; winter seasonal/vintage.
Comparison: more than a wheat Barleywine (expressive fruit/hops or oak complexity); less hop emphasis than American Barleywine.
Examples: The Bruery White Oak, Castelain Winter Ale, Perennial Heart of Gold, Two Brothers Bare Tree.

styles.name: Berliner Weisse
text: Aroma: moderate to mod-high sharp sour dominant; up to moderate fruitiness (lemon, tart apple, peach, apricot), light floral; NO hop aroma; raw bread dough/sourdough impression.

Flavor: clean lactic sourness dominates (can be strong), complementary doughy/bready wheat; hop bitterness undetectable; never vinegary; bright restrained fruit (apricot-peach, lemon, tart apple); very dry finish; no hop flavor; no THP.
Mouthfeel: light body but never thin; very high carbonation; no alcohol sensation; crisp acidity.
